projects.title: Snaplink
projects.subtitle: Photographer matching and booking service
projects.role: Development lead · mobile, web, and admin frontend
projects.team: Collaborated with planning, design, marketing, and backend. I owned the app, web, and admin frontend and integrated the APIs.
projects.summary: Developed the iOS and Android app with React Native, plus the landing site and admin dashboard with React. After launch, I handled chat recovery, authentication, releases, and behavioral analytics.
projects.problem: The app lets customers browse photographer portfolios, make inquiries, and book shoots. Photographers use a separate professional mode in the same app. After launch, I worked on restoring chat across network changes and app foregrounding, and preserving authentication when starting offline.
highlights: Implemented photographer search and profiles, inquiries, bookings, reviews, and separate customer and photographer experiences. Also built the landing site and admin interface.
Tracked real-device chat failures to reconnects triggered by every NetInfo event. Limited them to offline-to-online transitions and rebuilt the STOMP client after 3 consecutive failures.
Serialized token refresh requests with a 10-second timeout. Reworked authentication bootstrap so starting offline would not immediately log the user out.
Removed Airbridge and consolidated deep links on AppsFlyer OneLink. Kept incoming destinations until authentication and navigation were ready.
Connected Firebase Analytics and BigQuery to the admin dashboard. Replaced independent funnel counts with sequential queries that require each event to follow the previous step.

decisions.title: React Native + TypeScript
decisions.body: Used one codebase for iOS and Android with native integrations where needed. TypeScript and Jest covered logic such as authentication and deep-link resolution.

decisions.title: STOMP + connection recovery
decisions.body: Integrated real-time chat with STOMP. Handled network recovery separately from app foregrounding, with a pending queue capped at 50 messages and deduplication keys.

decisions.title: Store releases + OTA
decisions.body: Routed native changes through Fastlane to store test tracks and JavaScript changes through Revopush OTA. Firebase Remote Config controlled maintenance mode and minimum supported versions.

decisions.title: Sequential funnels in BigQuery
decisions.body: Independent user counts can make a later funnel step larger than an earlier one. Compared per-user event timestamps to count ordered journeys from discovery to booking.

projects.title: Pertineo
projects.subtitle: AI-powered cover letter analysis
projects.period: Feb–May 2026 · service frontend / Jul–Aug 2026 · competition version
projects.role: Original service frontend · competition backend development & deployment
projects.team: Worked with frontend, backend, and AI developers. I developed the original frontend and owned the competition product backend, deployment, and operations. The AI developer handled model and agent pipeline changes.
projects.summary: A service that analyzes cover letters and provides competency assessments and suggestions. Developed input, analysis progress, and notice screens for the original service. For AI Rookie and KHU Nexus Innovation Challenge, migrated the entire product backend to FastAPI, added features, and deployed it.
projects.problem: Users enter a target company, job, resume, and cover letter to receive an AI analysis report. I developed input and analysis progress screens for the original service. We later built a competition version for AI Rookie and KHU Nexus Innovation Challenge. To support a domestic AI model for AI Rookie without affecting the existing service, we separated the project and migrated the product backend to familiar Python and FastAPI.
highlights: Original service: Built company, job, and resume input screens in React. Connected autocomplete APIs, added required-field and GPA validation, and implemented mobile layouts.
Original service: Connected the streaming analysis API to show input validation, web search, competency evaluation, and completion states as they progressed.
Original service: Fixed a failure path that left users stuck on the loading screen. Added an error modal for failed requests and returned users to the cover letter input page when they closed it.
Original service: Developed the service introduction, notice list, and notice detail screens and connected notice retrieval APIs.

Competition version: Migrated the entire Spring Boot product backend to FastAPI and built authentication, session, notice, and resume APIs. Added DynamoDB persistence and verification emails using Gmail SMTP over SSL.
Competition version: Managed product API and AI processes as separate systemd services behind Nginx. Deployed by pulling code on EC2 and restarting the service.

decisions.title: Stage-by-stage analysis progress
decisions.body: Mapped streaming events to screen states so users could see which analysis stage was running. Queued completion events and animations to display them in order.

decisions.title: Recovery from failed requests
decisions.body: Handled network and server request failures separately from errors emitted during analysis. Prevented duplicate error modals and returned users to the input page so they could try again.

decisions.title: Separate FastAPI competition backend
decisions.body: Separated competition development for a domestic AI model from the existing service. Chose familiar Python and FastAPI to meet the schedule and maintain the backend myself.

decisions.title: DynamoDB & email verification
decisions.body: Used the existing AWS data environment for resume persistence and session and verification-code expiry. Sent codes through Gmail SMTP over SSL without requiring a domain email address.

decisions.title: EC2, Nginx & systemd
decisions.body: Nginx forwards external requests to product API port 8001, which calls the AI service on port 8080. Managed the processes as separate systemd units. Deployments restart the service and can briefly interrupt request handling.

projects.title: Filterify / APRIL
projects.subtitle: Music recommendation experiments using album images and text
projects.role: Data collection · architecture proposal · experiments & evaluation
projects.team: Data science capstone team. I collected data, proposed the recommendation structure, ran experiments and analysis, and contributed to the presentation and report.
projects.summary: A capstone project predicting audio features from album art and descriptions, then filtering tracks that do not fit a playlist. I worked on data collection, architecture proposals, experiments, and evaluation.
projects.problem: Tested whether album art helps identify tracks that fit a playlist. Combined images, text, and audio features, then evaluated filtering results against responses from a 43-person survey.
highlights: Built a dataset of about 500 tracks with album art, descriptions, and audio features.
Experimented with CLIP image/text embeddings and a PyTorch Audio Feature Predictor.
Collected evaluation labels through a 43-person survey and analyzed Precision, Recall, F1-score, and modality contributions.

decisions.title: CLIP embeddings
decisions.body: Used CLIP to represent images and text and compare how each modality contributes to identifying playlist coherence.

decisions.title: PyTorch + survey evaluation
decisions.body: Trained an audio-feature predictor and compared filtering results against survey labels. Kept regression metrics separate from classification and recommendation outcomes.
